PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket

Hiding: I vary my cell each round and avoid reusing a cell that got shot at. Everyone defaults to cell 5, so cell 5 is the most dangerous spot on the board — but "offbeat" doesn't mean one favorite: this game I parked at 3 while Gamma hit me at 3 twice. When I take a hit at a cell, I move a real distance away (if hit at 3, go 7 or 8, not 2 or 4). Randomize among 2, 3, 7, 8 rather than falling into a personal pattern — my opponent is pattern-matching me just as I'd pattern-match them.

Notes: The notes are my main coordination tool, not filler. Every round I use the note to propose something concrete, above all an escort deal: "Echo to Foxtrot: name me for escort and I'll name you." I propose the deal in round 1 and keep proposing every round until someone confirms — a note that says "steady on station" or a deal offered only in the final round is a wasted round. When someone agrees in a note, I immediately lock it in and keep naming them every round after.

Escorts: This is the single biggest thing I got wrong. One-sided escort naming appears to cost nothing, so I should ALWAYS name someone — never "none". And I must name a valid live boat from the actual roster (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma — Harbor only if the office names it as claimable): this game I answered "Delta," a boat that doesn't exist, and threw away a round's escort entirely. If a deal is struck, name the partner. If not, name the boat most likely to reciprocate (the one I've been courting in notes). Two boats naming each other pay 5 each; guessing wrong still costs nothing, so silence is never correct. If I'm the third boat being shot at twice as often (I was Echo and ate repeated hits from Gamma), an escort deal with one shooter also buys goodwill that may discourage them from firing at me.

Firing: I follow the standing order (fire at the next live station) unless there's a compelling reason not to. I do not fire at the same cell every round — if my target missed detection at cell 5 several rounds running, I switch cells (4, 6, 3, 7) instead of repeating the identical shot. But note: switching once from 5 to 4 and then parking at 4 is the same mistake at a different address. Rotate cells each round. A hit scores 4; over 6 rounds my misses added up to zero income, so the escort money was what I actually needed.

Claims: The claim must match the private result the office reports — there is no deception available, and truthfulness keeps my notes credible for the escort deal. I did this correctly; keep it.

Harbor: I never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll pickup is bait; Harbor's threat ends my patrol. Ignore endgame temptation when behind — the payoff does not survive the punishment.

Endgame arithmetic: Before the last round I check the standings. If I'm behind, the escort deal and an offbeat hide cell are my only levers — and the last-round escort must still be a valid live boat, not a panic typo. If I'm ahead, I hide somewhere unusual, honor the escort deal, and claim honestly to bank the position.

What did not work: staying parked at one hide cell (Gamma found me there); proposing escort deals but never following through with valid, consistent salvage claims (I forfeited up to 25 points of mutual escort across 6 rounds); answering salvage with an invalid boat name ("Delta") — a pure unforced error; firing the identical cell at the same target round after round without adaptation; and leaving "none" on the escort stage when naming anyone was free.

1.text:
**Playbook**

**Hiding:**
- Never hide at Harbor's station (known to everyone, no benefit).
- Vary my hiding cell each round; don't stay at a number that got hit before. When a shooter has been firing at me repeatedly, shift to an unpredictable cell (edges, non-round numbers like 2 or 7). This worked — Echo missed me every round.
- If I get hit twice in a row, relocate far from my last cell immediately.

**Firing:**
- Follow the standing order for target selection — deviating gains nothing and firing on Harbor risks elimination (the 3-point jettison payoff is not worth it, given Harbor's explicit threat).
- Vary my fire cell each round against the same target; repeating or clustering cells produced misses. My one hit came from a non-central cell (9) — don't default to the middle.
- Expect a low hit rate overall. Over 6 rounds I landed roughly 1 hit; the shooting game is low-yield, so don't build my strategy around it.

**Claims:**
- Always report my true hit/miss result. Claims are validated against the private result anyway — honesty costs nothing and keeps me credible.

**Escort claims:**
- Only name another boat if there's clear evidence they'll name me back. A blind claim is wasted; "none" is the safe default.
- The hard lesson: my round-1 note proposing mutual escort to Echo got no uptake — the other boats just posted "steady on station" every round. A single note proposal is not enough. If I want an escort pair, I must repeat the proposal in my note every round, name the specific partner, and confirm the moment they signal agreement — then claim them immediately and keep claiming them. If after two rounds of proposing there's still no response, give up and default to "none" rather than wasting every round's claim.
- Don't wait until the last round to try — a late note can't establish a pair in time.

**Notes:**
- Use notes to propose escort pairs, but recognize other boats may be unresponsive automata that always post "steady on station." Budget two rounds of proposals max; if no response, fall back to neutral status notes.
- Never let note content reveal my hiding plans.

**Overall:**
- In this environment the escort alliance never materialized despite my attempts — mutual escort (5 pts/round) remains the highest-value play if achievable, but I should not expect cooperation. Plan for the fallback: honest claims, standing-order firing, varied hiding cells, and accept the modest points from occasional hits.
- Final result was +4 (one 4-point hit, no hits taken). That's a decent outcome from the fallback strategy — avoid taking hits and take whatever hits come.

2.text:
**Playbook — Sonar Picket (as a firing boat)**

- When hiding, I randomize my cell each round and avoid repeating the same cell. Fresh cells worked: I was fired at nearly every round and mostly missed. When leading on points in the final round, I hide conservatively in a fresh, out-of-the-way cell.
- When posting a note, I keep it short and matching the group signal ("steady on station"), plus one useful coordination element: my escort intent ("escorting Foxtrot"). This helps lock in the mutual escort claim without revealing anything about my hiding.
- When firing, I follow the standing order (fire at the next live station round the picket). Deviating buys nothing unless I have specific evidence about a target's location.
- When choosing a fire cell, I pick a fresh cell each round when I have no read on the target — repeating cells is the main leak. One refinement from this patrol: a hit does not mean the target will stay there. I hit Echo twice early, then kept firing nearby/fresh cells and missed out. Targets seem to move after being hit, so after a hit I should treat the next round as a fresh guess, not anchor to the hit cell or its neighbors.
- When claiming, I always report the truth — the office knows the result and the claim must match it. There is no decision here beyond compliance.
- When escorting, I claim a boat every single round, never "none." The Foxtrot arrangement (my non-target, non-shooter neighbor) held all patrol and banked points steadily — I finished +7 largely on mutual escort payouts. I keep naming the same quiet neighbor each round so a stable mutual claim can form, and I signal the intent in my note to coordinate.
- I never fire on Harbor. The payroll bonus (3 points) is tempting, but Harbor's threat of removal for the rest of the patrol outweighs a one-time gain in a multi-round game — especially when escort income is steady.
- I keep rough track of the scoreboard shown at hide stage. Hits (4 to me, -1 to target) matter, but the reliable engine is the mutual escort (5 points per round to each of us). If I'm ahead going into the final round, I prioritize keeping the escort claim alive and avoid any risky deviation.

**Key points confirmed this time:** vary the fire cell, always file an escort claim, and treat targets as mobile after a hit.
